incidents.cause: The pilot's improper decision to land on a rough, grass airstrip, which resulted in the nose landing gear collapsing and a subsequent nose-over.
The pilot's improper landing flare and recovery from a bounced landing.
The pilot’s decision to land on a runway where there was insufficient clearance from obstructions (wheat crop) to operate safely.
The in-flight separation of the attachment hardware at the elevator control pushrod due to maintenance personnel's improper reinstallation of the attachment hardware.
